Paragraph: "Now, that invisible Seetha is intensifying my agony, and this visible spring season, the remover of the touch of sweat too, is doing the same...
Situation/Problem_Faced: Both the invisible (absent Seetha) and the visible (present spring) simultaneously work to intensify Rama's agony.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Rama points out how both absence and presence in his reality combine to produce grief.
Outcome/Resolution: He articulates the double burden on his emotional state.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Paroksha and Pratyaksha (The unperceived absence and perceived presence both causing emotional heat)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Demonstrates how both abstract loss (invisible Seetha) and concrete beauty (visible spring) push the mind toward deeper spiritual yearning.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Dual-trigger stress: internal mental thoughts (absence of loved one) and external sensory stimuli (pleasant weather) simultaneously aggravate psychological distress.
